strengths: Novel conceptual contribution: Reframing model collapse from a bug to a feature for machine unlearning is creative, well-motivated, and genuinely innovative
Privacy-preserving design: PMC's independence from ground-truth forget data addresses a fundamental conceptual and practical flaw in existing methods
Rigorous theoretical analysis with progression from categorical to practical LLMs (Lemma 1, Theorem 1 provide convergence guarantees)
Systematic identification of overlooked side effects in prior methods: distorted token probabilities in unrelated contexts (Figure 4a), information leakage in multiple-choice settings (Figures 4b-c)
Comprehensive fair experimental evaluation: 500 experiments per method (100 configurations × 5 seeds), Pareto front analysis, two model architectures
Robustness analysis against sampling and prefilling attacks demonstrates substantially better resilience than baselines
High reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters, datasets, ablation studies, and runtime analysis across appendices
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope: Evaluation only on TOFU (synthetic, fictional Q&A dataset); no results on real privacy/copyright scenarios. Questions about practical real-world applicability
Small model scale: Only tested on Phi-1.5 (1.5B) and Llama-3.2-3B; generalization to larger models (7B, 13B+) is unclear and important for modern applications
Computational overhead not sufficiently justified: 2× slower than baselines (40 min vs 20-30 min); marked as a 'bottleneck' but no analysis of acceptability for deployment

Task-dependent reward function design undermines generality: Experiments only explore one choice r(x)=1-ROUGE-L; limited exploration of how reward function affects performance and generalization across domains

Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes no statistical/function approximation errors; Bradley-Terry approximation (argmax vs sampling) justified only empirically; convergence guarantees may not hold in practice

Incomplete evaluation metrics: ROUGE-L only captures lexical overlap, not semantic unlearning; no human evaluation of response quality; multiple-choice scenarios use ChatGPT-generated rephrased answers which may not reflect real adversarial formulations
Missing robustness evaluation: No assessment against gradient-based attacks, membership inference, or other sophisticated extraction methods beyond sampling/prefilling
Utility degradation: 2-3% drops on ARC-Challenge/Arc-Easy/MMLU (Table 1) while 'minimal' could be significant for utility-critical applications

strengths: Novel conceptual framework connecting model collapse to machine unlearning, providing a creative perspective on an underexplored phenomenon
Privacy-conscious approach that avoids requiring ground-truth unlearning targets during the unlearning process itself
Comprehensive identification of three underexplored limitations in existing methods (token probability distortion, multiple-choice information leakage, sampling/prefilling vulnerabilities)
Strong empirical results showing PMC dominates baselines on utility-unlearning Pareto front across hyperparameter configurations
Excellent reproducibility practice with detailed hyperparameters, multiple random seeds, ablation studies, and promised code release
weaknesses: Substantial theory-practice gap: Theoretical analysis (Lemma 1, Theorem 1) assumes categorical distributions and zero statistical/function approximation errors, with tenuous connection to high-dimensional LLM unlearning; argmax approximation (τ→0) departs significantly from theoretical Bradley-Terry model

Severely limited experimental scope: single synthetic dataset (TOFU with 4K Q&A pairs about fictitious authors), small models (Phi-1.5, Llama-3.2-3B), one task type (Q&A only), no evaluation on real unlearning scenarios (copyrighted content, PII, malicious knowledge)

Computational overhead not justified: 50% runtime increase (30-40 vs 20-30 minutes) compared to baselines without clear practical benefit or compelling empirical justification for production deployment

Reward function design is critical but highly application-dependent and poorly explored; using ROUGE-L divergence is simplistic and may not generalize; no systematic ablation on reward function choices

Evaluation of side effects is somewhat anecdotal: multiple-choice leakage experiment on only 84 manually converted questions, sampling attacks use limited scope (100 samples), unclear if these represent realistic threat models, and NPO's low probabilities for forget answers may be intended behavior
Questionable privacy claims: claiming PMC avoids ground-truth unlearning targets is misleading since you still need to identify which questions to unlearn in practice, reducing the privacy advantage
Limited baseline comparisons: only 4 methods compared (GA, GD, NPO, SimNPO); missing recent preference optimization variants and methods specifically designed without requiring unlearning targets

Generalization questions unaddressed: how PMC scales to larger models (7B, 70B+), performs on other tasks/modalities, handles multi-turn conversations, or works when intended behavior is not 'I don't know'

Presentation could be clearer: dense notation without intuitive explanation, abrupt transition from categorical to GMMs to LLMs, and disconnect between theoretical formulations (Eqs 2-3) and practical algorithm (Algorithm 1)

strengths: Novel approach leveraging model collapse for machine unlearning is creative and well-motivated
Strong theoretical foundation with rigorous proofs for categorical and continuous distributions, progressing logically from theory to practice
Privacy-preserving design that avoids requiring ground-truth private data in the objective, addressing a genuine limitation of prior methods
Exceptionally thorough experimental evaluation: 500 experiments per method (100 configurations × 5 seeds), extensive ablations, fair baseline comparisons
Identifies and empirically validates real problems in existing methods: out-of-context token probability distortion, information leakage in multiple-choice settings, vulnerability to sampling attacks
Significantly expands Pareto frontier compared to baselines, achieving high unlearning quality while maintaining utility
Excellent reproducibility with detailed experimental setup, hyperparameters, runtime analysis, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited evaluation scope: only TOFU (synthetic Q&A) dataset; only question-answering tasks; only models ≤3B; untested on real-world datasets or other unlearning scenarios
Strong theoretical assumptions (no statistical/function approximation errors) that don't hold in practice; gap between theoretical guarantees and empirical LLM behavior not adequately addressed
Reward function design is ad-hoc and task-specific (ROUGE-L dissimilarity); limited guidance for practitioners on designing reward functions for different unlearning scenarios
Computational overhead (~50% vs baselines) with sampling as acknowledged bottleneck; no concrete solutions for efficiency explored
Theory-practice gap: Algorithm 1 uses argmax approximation instead of Bradley-Terry sampling; connection between theoretical Equation 2 and practical Algorithm 1 could be clearer
Multiple-choice evaluation limited to 84 questions with ChatGPT-generated distractors; relatively small evaluation set
Incomplete analyses: no testing when model never learned private information; limited ablation on number of samples n; no evaluation on larger models or diverse architectures

strengths: Novel conceptual reframing of model collapse as a feature for unlearning rather than a bug
Rigorous experimental validation with 500 experiments per method (100 configs × 5 seeds) across three LLM scales
Theoretical analysis providing formal guarantees for categorical distributions, with clear progression to continuous and practical LLM setting
Important empirical findings on side effects of prior methods: systematic token probability distortion in NPO (Figure 5a) and information leakage in multiple-choice settings
Superior robustness to sampling and prefilling attacks compared to baselines, addressing a real evaluation gap
Practical advantage of not requiring ground-truth forget answers, with genuine privacy benefits
Excellent reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters, extensive appendices, and code release promised
weaknesses: Theoretical assumptions are restrictive: Theorem 1 assumes non-zero probability mass on maximum reward without characterizing failure cases; for Phi-1.5 requires ≥10 samples per iteration, yet convergence to suboptimal rewards is not explained
Theorem 1 largely reiterates Ferbach et al. (2024) Lemma 2.2 rather than providing novel insight; significant gap between idealized theory and practical implementation

Unlearning definition is narrower than framed: focuses only on removing output information, not convergence to distributions like models never trained on forget data; Section 6's defense of this choice is somewhat evasive and unresolved

Unlearned outputs show problematic quality: converges to hallucinations, gibberish, or generic refusals (acknowledged in paper but left unresolved); raises questions about true 'unlearning' vs. degradation
Computational cost is non-trivial and higher than baselines: 40min (Phi-1.5), 20min (Llama), 200min (Gemma) due to sampling requirements; PMC-fast approximation sacrifices generality

Reward function design is under-explored and appears ad-hoc: ROUGE-L based metrics are simplistic, only self-BLEU explored as alternative (Appendix A.7), yet results heavily depend on reward choice with minimal design guidance

Unexplained utility degradation at collapse point (Figures 9-11): models appear not linearly mode-connected to originals; recovery mechanism unclear and questions connection to claimed convergence behavior
Severely limited generalization beyond Q&A: MUSE-news experiment explicitly called 'pilot study' with authors stating 'robust conclusions cannot be drawn'; main evaluation restricted to TOFU dataset

Evaluation metrics based on token overlap (ROUGE-L) rather than semantic similarity; models could produce semantically similar content with different tokens, conflating 'different syntax' with 'unlearned'

Critical assumption validation inadequate: why does Phi-1.5 require ≥10 samples to converge to optimal reward? Suboptimal convergence mechanism not analyzed; affects generalization of theoretical guarantees

strengths: Novel perspective connecting model collapse to machine unlearning with clear conceptual motivation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including extensive ablations, multiple models, and robustness analysis
Identified concrete side effects in baseline methods (token probability distortion, multiple-choice leakage)
Avoids requiring ground-truth forget sequences during unlearning, addressing privacy concerns
Formal theoretical analysis with convergence guarantees for categorical distributions and reward optimization
weaknesses: Fundamental problem definition: Solves output-level unlearning rather than standard distribution-convergence unlearning without adequately justifying sufficiency
Significant theory-practice gap: Theoretical results assume no approximation errors (unrealistic); jump from categorical distributions to LLMs not formally justified
Reward function design is critical but underexplored: ROUGE-L choice appears arbitrary, only two variants tested, no principled guidance for practitioners on selection
Output quality unaddressed: Convergence to hallucinations/gibberish acknowledged but not solved; paper sidesteps rather than addresses generation coherence
Limited evaluation scope: Only TOFU benchmark (fictional data, 400 forget samples); no real copyright/privacy scenarios; authors acknowledge MUSE-news experiments are insufficient

Statistical rigor issues: Single runs for Gemma-3-12b due to computational cost; gradient checkpointing instability (A.9) causes different trajectories; missing baseline comparisons for largest models
Incomplete unlearning evaluation: No membership inference attacks or privacy tests; ROUGE-L similarity is weak guarantee against alternative information encodings
Utility degradation at collapse point indicates convergence to non-linearly-connected model; unclear whether this achieves true unlearning
Computational costs non-trivial (Phi: 40 min, Gemma: 200 min) and sampling overhead not fully accounted for
Modest technical novelty: Bradley-Terry model borrowed from prior work; Algorithm 1 is straightforward despite conceptual innovation

strengths: Novel approach reframing model collapse as a feature for unlearning with clear practical motivation
Solid theoretical contributions with rigorous analysis of categorical and general distributions
Exceptionally thorough experimental evaluation: 500 experiments per method (100 configs × 5 seeds) across three LLMs
Important findings identifying side effects in existing methods (distorted probabilities, information leakage in multiple-choice settings)
Superior robustness to sampling and prefilling attacks compared to strong baselines
Clear practical advantages: no requirement for ground-truth sequences, better privacy properties, preserves generation on unrelated contexts
Comprehensive ablations and appendices supporting reproducibility
Honest discussion of limitations and theory-practice gaps
weaknesses: Theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 assumes no approximation errors, which doesn't hold for practical LLMs; formal error bounds absent
Weak formal privacy guarantees; focuses on empirical output-level unlearning rather than formal privacy definitions (e.g., differential privacy)
Evaluation primarily on synthetic TOFU dataset; real-world unlearning behavior may differ; MUSE-news evaluation acknowledged as insufficient
Generation quality issues (hallucinations, gibberish, generic refusals) inadequately addressed; impacts user experience and deployability
Convergence requires non-zero probability on maximum-reward responses; convergence to suboptimal rewards when this assumption fails (Appendix A.4)
Reward function design is application-specific; limited guidance for practitioners; ROUGE-L metric captures only surface-level similarity
Gradient checkpointing introduces substantial uncontrolled variance (Appendix A.9), raising reproducibility concerns across systems
Sharp utility drops at collapse point across all methods; recovery trajectory unclear; potential non-connectivity to original model
Limited scope: primarily Q&A tasks; scalability to large models (100B+) untested; computational cost not negligible relative to baselines
